questions.question_text: In an ARM template, which section defines the list of parameters that can be passed during deployment?
questions.explanation: The 'parameters' section declares parameters, their type, default values, and constraints, allowing them to be supplied at deployment time.

questions.question_text: In a Bicep file, which syntax correctly assigns a location value to a resource?
questions.explanation: Bicep uses the colon (:) to assign values, so 'location: 'eastus'' is the proper syntax.

questions.question_text: Which Azure CLI command deploys a Bicep file named main.bicep to a resource group called rg1?

options.label: A
options.text: az deployment group create --resource-group rg1 --template-file main.bicep

options.label: C
options.text: az deployment sub create --resource-group rg1 --template-file main.bicep

questions.explanation: The az deployment group create command with --template-file is used to deploy a Bicep or ARM template to a specified resource group.

questions.question_text: How can you export an existing Azure resource to an ARM template using Azure CLI?
questions.explanation: The az resource export command exports the specified resource and its dependencies into an ARM template file.

questions.question_text: In a Bicep file, which keyword is used to reference a parameter's value?
questions.explanation: The @ symbol prefixes a parameter name to reference its value within expressions, e.g., @parameters.location.

questions.question_text: You need to change the SKU of a virtual machine resource from 'Standard_B1s' to 'Standard_D2s' in a Bicep file. Which line should you edit?
questions.explanation: The SKU property within the resource definition should be updated to 'sku: 'Standard_D2s'' (or the full resource block), and option D shows the correct line to modify.

questions.question_text: Which of the following is required to successfully deploy a Bicep file that references an external module?

options.label: A
options.text: The module file must be in the same directory as the main Bicep file

options.label: B
options.text: The module must be uploaded to an Azure Storage account and referenced by its blob URL

options.label: C
options.text: The module must be included in the same Bicep file

options.label: D
options.text: The module must be defined as a parameter

questions.explanation: External modules are typically stored in a storage account and referenced via a blob URL, allowing reuse across deployments.

questions.question_text: What does the 'outputs' section of an ARM template define?

options.label: C
options.text: Values that are returned after deployment

questions.explanation: Outputs expose values (such as resource IDs or IPs) after deployment, making them available to downstream processes or users.

questions.question_text: When using Bicep, how can you conditionally create a resource based on a boolean parameter named 'enableLogging'?
questions.explanation: Bicep supports conditional resource creation using the 'if' keyword directly after the resource type, e.g., resource 'Microsoft.Whatever' = if (enableLogging) { ... }.

questions.question_text: Which Azure CLI command deploys an ARM template stored in a GitHub repository to a resource group?

options.label: A
options.text: az deployment group create --resource-group rg1 --template-uri https://github.com/.../template.json

options.label: D
options.text: az deployment sub create --resource-group rg1 --template-uri https://github.com/.../template.json

questions.explanation: The az deployment group create command with --template-uri points to a remote template (e.g., a GitHub URL) and deploys it to the specified resource group.
